question: Why do many FGM survivors hesitate to speak up about their sexual and mental struggles?

options.A: Psychological symptoms disappear completely after marriage
options.B: Cultural taboos make discussing female sexuality difficult
options.C: Hospitals routinely provide mandatory counseling at birth
options.D: Mental health professionals are legally banned from treating women

explanation: Strict societal taboos around sex and reproductive parts force many women to hide their pain and suffer in silence. As a nurse, your gentle care creates a safe space for them.

question: Why is checking a new medication order faster on an EMR than using paper?

options.A: The pharmacy sees the order on the screen the moment it is entered
options.B: The computer system automatically injects the medication for the nurse
options.C: Doctors are no longer allowed to prescribe medications on paper
options.D: Paper charts are kept locked off-site in a secure bank vault

explanation: No more running physical paper down to the pharmacy! Instant network sharing saves valuable time in busy clinical settings.

question: What is the best advice for a nurse to give a patient who just had a cervical polypectomy?

options.A: Expect heavy bleeding equivalent to a heavy period
options.B: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampons for a short time
options.C: Douching daily is required to prevent local infection
options.D: Remain on complete bed rest for one full week

explanation: Giving the cervix a little break from anything inserted vaginally lets the small surgical site heal up nicely and safely.

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to create a private, gentle setting during a perineal check?

options.A: Bright lighting interferes with visualizing superficial blood vessels
options.B: Perineal tissue is too fragile to touch without numbing agents
options.C: Patients frequently feel embarrassed about intimate examinations
options.D: Hospital policy strictly forbids family members from staying

explanation: Checking someone's private areas can feel very vulnerable. As a caring nurse, building trust and keeping things private helps your patient feel safe and respected.

question: What is the main difference between vaccine efficacy and vaccine effectiveness?

options.A: Effectiveness applies only to viral vaccines while efficacy applies to bacterial vaccines
options.B: Effectiveness is determined in a laboratory before animal testing begins
options.C: Efficacy measures performance in ideal trials while effectiveness measures performance in everyday settings
options.D: Efficacy is measured in children while effectiveness is measured in adults

explanation: Think of efficacy as how a vaccine performs in a controlled lab test, while effectiveness is how it holds up for real people out in the community! You've got this.

question: What special feature in modern surgical swabs helps find them easily on an X-ray?

options.A: A built-in electronic tracking chip
options.B: A bright fluorescent dye coating
options.C: A radiopaque marker strip
options.D: A magnetic metallic button

explanation: Radiopaque strips show up brightly on X-ray machines, acting like a safety net if a swab ever goes missing.

question: What percentage of pre-pregnancy weight loss is typically used to help define hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: Exactly 10%
options.B: Greater than 5%
options.C: Less than 1%
options.D: Around 20%

explanation: Losing more than 5 percent of pre-pregnancy body weight due to continuous vomiting points strongly toward hyperemesis gravidarum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h2)

question: What does the term intersectionality describe in patient care?

options.A: The physical meeting point where blood vessels cross in the body
options.B: The exact moment when a patient transitions from childhood to adulthood
options.C: How multiple social identities overlap to shape unique life experiences
options.D: How biological sex interacts strictly with inherited genetic diseases

explanation: Intersectionality highlights that factors like race, gender, and class combine to influence a person's unique health realities and challenges. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is it called when a baby's head is simply too big to fit through the mother's pelvis?

options.A: Uterine inversion
options.B: Breech presentation
options.C: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: Don't let the big words scare you: 'cephalic' means head, 'pelvic' means pelvis, and 'disproportion' means a size mismatch between the two!

question: Why is a community diagnosis considered an ongoing cycle rather than a single event?

options.A: Because government funding stops after the first month
options.B: Because health needs change and progress must be evaluated
options.C: Because nurses are required to rewrite reports every week
options.D: Because community members refuse to answer questions twice

explanation: Communities change over time, and nurses must continuously evaluate whether interventions are working and what new problems have arisen. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which correlation coefficient shows the strongest relationship between two variables?

options.A: plus 0.10
options.B: zero point zero five
options.C: minus 0.40
options.D: minus 0.85

explanation: Spot on! Ignore the minus sign for a moment—0.85 is the furthest away from zero, which means it has the strongest punch!

question: Why is diet therapy such an important part of your daily nursing duties?

options.A: Nurses must personally cook all meals served in the hospital ward
options.B: Nurses are responsible for monitoring patient tolerance and supporting the prescribed nutrition plan
options.C: Dietary plans replace the need for physical assessments
options.D: Doctors never check what patients are eating

explanation: Since you spend the most time with patients, you are in the best position to see if they are enjoying their food and how well their body is handling it!

question: Why is chronic kidney disease an important thing to note when taking a patient's blood history?

options.A: It triggers sudden and uncontrollable blood clotting
options.B: Damaged kidneys produce less erythropoietin, causing anaemia
options.C: It causes the liver to stop storing iron completely
options.D: Kidney failure immediately destroys all white blood cells

explanation: Healthy kidneys make erythropoietin, the hormone that tells the bone marrow to build red blood cells. When kidneys fail, that hormone drops, leading to anaemia.

question: An emergency ward is trying out a new documentation tool. What action will best help the staff adopt it successfully?

options.A: Forcing staff to use the exact original tool without listening to their feedback
options.B: Hiding the tool instructions until every nurse has completed a written exam
options.C: Allowing the emergency nurses to adapt the tool slightly to fit their fast-paced workflow
options.D: Punishing any nurse who forgets to use the tool during the first week

explanation: Flexibility is key! When staff get to shape how a tool fits their busy shift, they feel proud and are much more likely to use it.

question: Why is it important to write down any learning barriers (like poor eyesight or hearing) in the nursing notes?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal handovers between shifts
options.B: It allows the hospital to charge extra fees for communication
options.C: It guides incoming nurses on how to adapt future teaching sessions
options.D: It proves the patient was difficult and uncooperative

explanation: Documenting barriers helps the whole nursing team communicate effectively without making the patient repeat themselves. Excellent teamwork!

question: What is the difference between intragroup and intergroup conflict?

options.A: Intragroup involves money, while intergroup involves medical errors.
options.B: Intragroup happens within the same team, while intergroup happens between different teams.
options.C: Intragroup is internal, while intergroup is external.
options.D: Intragroup only occurs at night, while intergroup occurs during the day.

explanation: Think of 'intra-' as *within* one group, and 'inter-' as *between* separate groups. Easy trick to remember!

question: A patient is dealing with loneliness and money troubles after losing their partner. What do these life events represent?

options.A: Genetic and chromosomal mutations
options.B: Environmental and situational stressors
options.C: Primary endocrine abnormalities
options.D: Congenital brain structural defects

explanation: You nailed it! Things happening in a person's surroundings—like loss, isolation, or financial stress—are situational triggers that can spark depression.

question: Why is mixing minor tranquilizers with alcohol so dangerous?

options.A: Both substances slow down the nervous system and can cause breathing to stop
options.B: Alcohol chemically neutralizes the drug and causes sudden seizures
options.C: It triggers severe allergic skin rashes across the body
options.D: The combination permanently damages liver enzymes instantly

explanation: Both alcohol and minor tranquilizers are central nervous system depressants. Combined, they can dangerously shut down a person's breathing.

question: Why is sharing your computer login password with a colleague during a busy shift dangerous?

options.A: It locks the computer hardware permanently until IT resets it
options.B: It automatically deletes all patient lab reports in the system
options.C: It slows down the hospital internet connection speed significantly
options.D: It breaks accountability because actions under that login are tied to your name

explanation: Every action in an EHR is logged against the active user account, so sharing credentials destroys reliable audit trails. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h4)

question: A patient has severe swelling around both eyes from a facial injury, making it impossible for them to open their eyes. How should you document the eye score?

options.A: Force the eyelids open to check for a spontaneous score
options.B: Record a score of 4 because they might open them later
options.C: Record a score of 2 because swelling counts as pain
options.D: Note eye opening as untestable due to swelling

explanation: Never force swollen eyelids open! Always document that the eye score is untestable due to local trauma or edema, keeping your patient safe and comfortable.

question: Why is hiding medical mistakes a bad idea in nursing?

options.A: It prevents nurses from charting properly
options.B: It increases the cost of hospital equipment
options.C: It always leads to immediate license revocation
options.D: It deepens trauma and damages patient trust

explanation: Hiding mistakes only makes things worse. It causes more emotional pain for families and completely destroys their trust in us as healthcare providers.

question: Which of these is NOT a requirement for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) to work safely?

options.A: The baby must be exclusively breastfed
options.B: The infant must be older than one year
options.C: The infant must be under six months of age
options.D: The mother must not have resumed menstruation

explanation: LAM is a temporary method that only works for the first six months after birth, as long as breastfeeding is exclusive and periods haven't returned.

question: Why is 'replication' (repeating a study) so important in scientific nursing research?

options.A: It proves that the researcher is more important than the clinician
options.B: It helps verify whether original results were accurate and reliable
options.C: It eliminates the need for patient consent in clinical trials
options.D: It ensures that hospital policies never change again

explanation: When different researchers repeat a study and get the same results, we can trust that the findings are solid and dependable.

question: Around the sixth day after delivery, what kind of vaginal discharge is most normal to see?

options.A: Bright red clots
options.B: Clear watery fluid
options.C: Pinkish-brown discharge
options.D: Yellowish-white creamy discharge

explanation: Brilliant! As healing continues, lochia changes from red to a thinner, pinkish-brown fluid called lochia serosa around days five through nine.

question: Why should patients always be involved in setting their own rehabilitation goals?

options.A: It ensures the recovery targets matter to the patient's actual daily life.
options.B: It completely removes the need for physical therapy oversight.
options.C: Hospital accreditation rules legally prohibit nurse-only care plans.
options.D: Patients have medical degrees that guide clinical interventions.

explanation: Exactly! When patients help choose what they want to achieve, they feel more motivated to push through tough therapy sessions.

question: Why is avoiding a fever important for a patient recovering from cardiac arrest?

options.A: Fever stops the heart from responding to standard medications
options.B: Fever increases the brain's need for oxygen and worsens injury
options.C: Fever causes the intravenous lines to clot off quickly
options.D: Fever makes it impossible to check the patient's blood pressure

explanation: Elevated temperatures speed up brain metabolism when brain cells are already vulnerable, leading to worse recovery outcomes. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h7)

question: What is the first thing you should do when building a histogram from raw numbers?

options.A: Calculate the exact average of the categorical groups
options.B: Find the range by identifying the lowest and highest values
options.C: Color the bars using alternating bright shades
options.D: Draw the vertical and horizontal axes freehand

explanation: You always want to know your lowest and highest numbers first so you know how wide your chart needs to stretch!

question: What should you do right after the AED delivers a shock?

options.A: Resume chest compressions immediately.
options.B: Wait for the doctor to arrive and give orders.
options.C: Check for a carotid pulse for ten seconds.
options.D: Remove the electrode pads from the chest.

explanation: Don't wait to check for a pulse right after a shock! Jump right back into chest compressions to keep that blood moving.

question: What kind of metabolic shift is typically triggered by major trauma, severe burns, or sepsis?

options.A: Metabolic dormancy
options.B: Hypermetabolic state
options.C: Basal stabilization
options.D: Hypometabolic hibernation

explanation: 'Hyper' means high! Severe physical stress forces the body into overdrive to fight off infection and heal wounds quickly.

question: What is the main limitation of an Electronic Medical Record (EMR) compared to an EHR?

options.A: It is usually restricted to a single facility or clinic
options.B: It cannot be viewed by registered nurses or doctors
options.C: It only contains billing information and insurance forms
options.D: It is always written on paper rather than typed digitally

explanation: Good job! An EMR is great for one specific clinic's digital files, but it doesn't easily share that info with outside hospitals.

question: How does stomach acid help protect you from getting sick?

options.A: By coating the intestinal lining with a thick mucus
options.B: By destroying ingested bacteria and other microorganisms
options.C: By producing specific antibodies against food antigens
options.D: By stimulating the production of white blood cells

explanation: Exactly! The strong acid in your stomach acts like a harsh chemical bath that kills most of the germs you accidentally swallow with your food or water.

question: A patient has a stubborn, hard mass of stool that normal enemas can't shift. What procedure is best here?

options.A: A rectal washout
options.B: An intravenous fluid bolus
options.C: A nasogastric tube insertion
options.D: An oral laxative challenge

explanation: When standard enemas aren't strong enough to break up severe blockages, a rectal washout provides the extra mechanical help needed.

question: Why do adults in a holoendemic community often show no symptoms of the disease?

options.A: The local climate prevents the disease germ from surviving in adults
options.B: They caught the infection and built immunity during early childhood
options.C: Adult bodies naturally destroy the germ before it can enter the blood
options.D: Traditional herbal medicines protect adults from getting sick

explanation: In holoendemic settings, almost everyone gets infected very early in life, leaving surviving adults with strong long-term immunity. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h1)

question: Which of the following items is classified specifically as sharps waste?

options.A: Bloody surgical gowns
options.B: Expired oral tablets
options.C: Contaminated cotton balls
options.D: Used scalpel blades

explanation: Sharps include items like blades and needles that can easily puncture skin and transmit infections. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h2)

question: What legal document outlines a patient's specific wishes regarding life-sustaining medical treatments?

options.A: A hospital discharge summary sheet
options.B: A physician prescription log
options.C: An advance directive or living will
options.D: A standard health insurance claim form

explanation: Living wills and advance directives legally document a person's preferences for medical interventions when they can no longer speak for themselves. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h7)

question: How do non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) help relieve pain?

options.A: Blocking prostaglandins to reduce pain and swelling
options.B: Destroying bacteria directly in the bloodstream
options.C: Permanently stopping all white blood cell production
options.D: Freezing the skin to numb local nerve endings

explanation: You nailed it! NSAIDs stop the body from making prostaglandins, which are the chemical messengers of pain and swelling.

question: Why do some women experience upset stomach or diarrhoea along with their menstrual cramps?

options.A: The uterus physically presses directly against the stomach and bowels
options.B: Infection spreads rapidly from the pelvis to the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Prostaglandins enter the bloodstream and affect other body systems
options.D: Hormonal shifts cause a sudden increase in daily food poisoning rates

explanation: Exactly! Prostaglandins don't just stay in the uterus; when they travel through the bloodstream, they can also stimulate the digestive tract.

question: What does 'horizontal equity' mean for patients?

options.A: All nurses must earn the exact same monthly salary
options.B: Hospitals must be built in straight lines across geographical zones
options.C: People with equal health needs must be treated equally
options.D: Wealthy individuals must pay for the healthcare of rural farmers

explanation: Horizontal equity means if two patients walk in with the exact same health problem, they get the same quality of care.

question: Which of these common phrases should a nurse avoid saying to someone who is grieving?

options.A: I am here for you whenever you want to talk
options.B: I am so sorry for your loss
options.C: Time heals all wounds
options.D: It is okay to cry if you need to

explanation: Phrases like 'time heals all wounds' can feel dismissive and unhelpful. Instead, just let them know you are there for them.

question: What happens when bacteria become resistant to older, cheaper antibiotics?

options.A: Doctors have to switch to more expensive or stronger alternative drugs
options.B: Pharmacies stop stocking antibacterial medications altogether
options.C: Patients require fewer laboratory tests before starting therapy
options.D: Infections disappear faster because bacteria become weaker over time

explanation: When cheap first-line drugs fail, patients face higher costs and sometimes harsher treatments. That's why fighting resistance is so crucial!

question: What is a major difference between vitamins and macronutrients like carbs and fats?

options.A: Vitamins are only used to build bones.
options.B: Vitamins are needed in much larger amounts.
options.C: Vitamins cannot be found in natural foods.
options.D: Vitamins do not supply calories.

explanation: Vitamins are vital for health, but unlike carbs, fats, and proteins, they don't give us energy or calories. They have other super important jobs!

question: What is the main focus of a National Drug Policy compared to a general health policy?

options.A: Pharmaceuticals and medicine supply chains
options.B: Medical doctor and nurse salary structures
options.C: Hospital building construction and maintenance
options.D: Global health donor funding negotiations

explanation: Think of it this way: while a general health policy looks at everything in healthcare, a National Drug Policy zooms in specifically on medicines—making sure they are produced, distributed, and used safely!

question: What is the primary goal of food purchasing in nutritional care?

options.A: Minimizing the time spent on meal preparation
options.B: Reducing the variety of meals served daily
options.C: Buying the most expensive ingredients available
options.D: Ensuring access to safe and nutrient-dense foods

explanation: Food purchasing aims to acquire safe, wholesome ingredients that supply the necessary nutrients for good health. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h1)

question: After teaching a patient about wound care, what must the nurse document in the patient's notes?

options.A: Nothing, as verbal education does not require charting
options.B: Details of what was taught, the method used, and the patient's response
options.C: A summary of the nurse's personal feelings about the patient
options.D: Only the date and the nurse's personal signature

explanation: Well done! If it wasn't charted, legally it wasn't done. Always record what you taught and how the patient responded.

question: Which set of organs belongs to the internal structures of the male reproductive system?

options.A: Prepuce and glans penis
options.B: Scrotal skin and dartos muscle
options.C: Testes and accessory glands
options.D: Scrotum and penile shaft

explanation: Internal structures include the testes, duct system, and accessory glands, while the scrotum and penis are external. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h1)

question: When wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) during an outbreak, what is a common hazard nurses need to watch out for?

options.A: Contaminating oneself while taking off the gear incorrectly
options.B: Causing the laboratory printer to jam during data entry
options.C: Forgetting to check the expiration date on the patient's chart
options.D: Catching a cold from the air conditioning in the isolation room

explanation: You got it! Taking off (doffing) PPE the wrong way is one of the easiest ways healthcare workers accidentally contaminate themselves.

question: A mum in long labour has dry lips, dark urine, and a fast pulse. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Prepare the patient for immediate vaginal delivery
options.B: Encourage her to perform heavy physical exercises
options.C: Start an intravenous infusion to correct dehydration
options.D: Restrict all fluids to prevent vomiting

explanation: Spot on! Those signs clearly point to dehydration. Setting up an IV line quickly restores her strength and helps her uterine muscles keep working.

question: Which group of occupational lung diseases is caused by inhaling mineral dusts like silica and asbestos?

options.A: Pneumoconiosis
options.B: Simple Bronchitis
options.C: Occupational Asthma
options.D: Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis

explanation: Pneumoconiosis is the medical term for fibrotic lung diseases caused by the accumulation of mineral dusts in the lungs. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h3)

question: How do Mastomys rats spread the Lassa virus around?

options.A: By biting humans aggressively during daylight hours
options.B: By carrying ticks that drop onto human skin
options.C: By shedding the virus in their urine, faeces, and saliva
options.D: Through respiratory droplets when they sneeze or cough

explanation: Even though the rats don't look sick, their droppings and urine constantly contaminate food items and household surfaces.

question: Which group of patients is usually most at risk for catching hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Athletes with minor muscular sprains
options.B: Children with mild seasonal allergies
options.C: Healthy young adults visiting friends
options.D: Elderly patients receiving immune-suppressing medications

explanation: Correct! Older age plus medications that lower immunity make these patients much more vulnerable to infections.

question: A patient with a fungal skin infection in the groin area asks how to prevent spreading it and getting it again. What should the nurse advise?

options.A: Apply thick occlusive petroleum jelly over the area all day
options.B: Wash the skin vigorously with harsh antiseptic soap every hour
options.C: Keep the skin folds clean and dry, and do not share towels
options.D: Wear heavy synthetic clothing to trap warm air near the skin

explanation: Fungi thrive in warm, moist places, so keeping the skin dry and avoiding shared personal items like towels stops transmission and growth. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T10#GNS213_U5_T10_h5)

question: Which of these is a very common nursing diagnosis for a patient struggling with a severe phobia?

options.A: Impaired Gas Exchange
options.B: Deficient Fluid Volume
options.C: Risk for Infection
options.D: Ineffective Coping

explanation: Because phobias rely heavily on avoidance rather than healthy problem-solving, 'Ineffective Coping' fits right in your care plan.

question: Which substance builds up in the joints to trigger a painful gout attack?

options.A: Infected purulent white blood cells
options.B: Monosodium urate crystals
options.C: Excess synovial lubricating fluid
options.D: Calcium pyrophosphate deposits

explanation: Gout happens when excess uric acid forms sharp, needle-like crystals (monosodium urate) in the joint space. Ouch! That's what causes that sudden, intense pain.

question: Why can a problem at the very start of hormone production affect multiple different hormone levels?

options.A: All sex hormones share a common pathway originating from cholesterol.
options.B: Adrenal glands stop producing blood entirely.
options.C: Receptors on target tissues become permanently blocked.
options.D: The liver destroys excess hormones when one pathway fails.

explanation: Since all sex hormones branch out from the same starting block (cholesterol), a hiccup early in the chain reaction alters everything downstream. Makes total sense when you picture it like a branching river!

question: Which external structure is a small, highly sensitive erectile organ?

options.A: Labia majora
options.B: Mons pubis
options.C: Clitoris
options.D: Bartholin gland

explanation: The clitoris sits at the top of the labia minora and contains many nerve endings for sexual sensation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which diagnostic imaging tool is most commonly used to identify structural brain abnormalities in a child with suspected cerebral palsy?

options.A: Abdominal ultrasound
options.B: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.C: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
options.D: Standard chest X-ray

explanation: An MRI provides detailed images of brain tissue, helping clinicians identify areas of past injury or malformation. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h5)

question: A patient has hearing loss because the sensory hair cells inside their cochlea are damaged. What type of hearing loss is this?

options.A: Central auditory processing deficit
options.B: Mixed obstructive hearing loss
options.C: Sensorineural hearing loss
options.D: Conductive hearing loss

explanation: When the issue lies in the inner ear hair cells or the auditory nerve itself, we call it sensorineural hearing loss. It is usually permanent, but hearing aids or implants can help patients connect with sounds again.

question: What is the highest possible value for a correlation coefficient?

options.A: zero
options.B: plus or minus 100
options.C: plus or minus 1.00
options.D: infinity

explanation: Well done! Correlation numbers always stay neatly between -1.00 and +1.00.

question: How do Volkmann's canals differ in direction from Haversian canals?

options.A: Volkmann's run horizontally, while Haversian run vertically
options.B: Volkmann's are microscopic, while Haversian are visible to the eye
options.C: Volkmann's are found in spongy bone, while Haversian are in compact bone
options.D: Volkmann's carry nerves only, while Haversian carry blood only

explanation: Spot on! Volkmann's run across horizontally, linking up nicely with the vertical central (Haversian) canals inside the osteons.

question: What is the main job of a control chart in healthcare quality improvement?

options.A: To track data over time and spot abnormal process changes
options.B: To calculate the exact hourly salary of nursing personnel
options.C: To punish staff members when medication errors increase
options.D: To schedule upcoming staff leave during holiday periods

explanation: Well done! Control charts help us look at data chronologically so we can easily tell normal daily ups and downs apart from real problems.

question: How do gentle laxatives usually differ from strong purgatives?

options.A: Laxatives cause rapid and violent fluid evacuation of the bowel
options.B: Laxatives produce softer, more formed stools with less urgency
options.C: Laxatives can only be administered through intravenous lines
options.D: Laxatives completely paralyze the smooth muscle of the colon

explanation: Think of laxatives as gentle helpers for mild relief, whereas strong purgatives bring fast, watery results!

question: What is the primary reason patients with chronic malabsorption develop peripheral edema?

options.A: Loss of plasma proteins leading to decreased blood oncotic pressure
options.B: Direct blockage of the lymphatic vessels inside the lower extremities
options.C: Excessive retention of salt caused by overactive adrenal glands
options.D: Increased pumping pressure generated by a weakened heart muscle

explanation: When the gut fails to absorb protein, blood albumin drops. This lowers blood oncotic pressure, allowing fluid to leak out of vessels into body tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h6)

question: Which lifestyle change is a major reason diabetes is becoming more common in Nigerian cities?

options.A: Engaging in heavy manual farm labor every morning
options.B: Consuming excessive amounts of natural spring water
options.C: Increasing daily intake of green leafy vegetables
options.D: Adopting processed diets and reducing physical activity

explanation: With busy city life, more people eat fast, processed foods and move around less. This shift in lifestyle greatly increases metabolic risks. Great insight for community nursing!

question: What must happen for a child to be born with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Only the mother needs to have the full sickle cell disease
options.B: The child must be exposed to severe malaria during infancy
options.C: Both parents must pass on a copy of the mutated sickle cell gene
options.D: Either parent must have genotype AS while the other has genotype AA

explanation: Because it is an autosomal recessive condition, a child needs two copies of the abnormal gene, requiring both parents to contribute a sickle gene. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h2)

question: Why is 'recency error' a bad thing during an annual nursing review?

options.A: It forces the manager to use outdated hospital policies from years ago
options.B: It ignores months of good or bad work and focuses only on recent events
options.C: It requires the nurse to memorize every shift worked in the past month
options.D: It increases the time needed to complete the final paperwork

explanation: It's unfair to judge a whole year of hard work based only on what happened in the last two weeks. Managers need to look at the big picture!

question: How do prospective study findings directly benefit frontline nurses working in clinical wards?

options.A: By providing historical background on ancient medical discoveries
options.B: By eliminating the need for patient assessments during night shifts
options.C: By replacing all bedside charting with automated computer algorithms
options.D: By helping identify high-risk patients early so preventative nursing care can be applied

explanation: Prospective research uncovers risk factors that frontline nurses use to spot vulnerable patients and prevent adverse hospital events. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h7)

question: Why do women who have undergone infibulation frequently suffer from recurrent urinary tract infections?

options.A: Urine pools behind the scar tissue and narrow opening, promoting bacterial growth.
options.B: Frequent catheterization is required for basic hygiene.
options.C: The procedure permanently destroys the kidneys' ability to filter waste.
options.D: Hormonal imbalances alter the natural pH of the bladder.

explanation: A constricted or partially blocked urinary outlet prevents complete bladder emptying, leaving residual urine that easily harbors bacteria. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which everyday nursing action relies most directly on the discovery of germ theory?

options.A: Helping the patient perform passive range of motion exercises
options.B: Performing strict hand hygiene and surgical asepsis
options.C: Documenting vital signs every four hours on the bedside chart
options.D: Assessing the patient's nutritional status and dietary intake

explanation: Handwashing and sterile techniques are our frontline defense to stop germs from spreading between patients. Pure nursing basics!

question: What is the primary function of the microscopic microvilli lining the proximal convoluted tubule?

options.A: To increase surface area for reabsorbing substances
options.B: To push urine upward toward the renal cortex
options.C: To trap large red blood cells before filtration
options.D: To secrete excess white blood cells into the filtrate

explanation: Microvilli create a brush border that greatly expands the surface area available to pull water and nutrients back into the blood. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why do nurse researchers collect data in a study?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside shift reports completely
options.B: To prove that a chosen nursing theory is entirely wrong
options.C: To fulfill mandatory paperwork requirements for the hospital
options.D: To gather information needed to answer a research question

explanation: Think of data collection like gathering clues to solve a case. You collect specific info to answer your main research question!

question: Which phase of disaster management involves strengthening hospital buildings so they can survive an earthquake?

options.A: Mitigation
options.B: Response
options.C: Recovery
options.D: Triage

explanation: Mitigation is all about taking action *before* a disaster strikes to reduce damage and keep people safe.

question: What is a key responsibility of the psychiatric nurse in continuing care?

options.A: Managing hospital finances and staff payroll budgets
options.B: Observing mental status and evaluating medication side effects
options.C: Prescribing brand new antipsychotic drugs independently
options.D: Diagnosing rare surgical disorders in the community

explanation: Nurses closely monitor how the patient is doing mentally and check for any troublesome reactions to prescribed drugs. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why is using strategic silence during an interview actually a great communication tool?

options.A: It shows the researcher is bored with the conversation
options.B: It gives the participant time to think and share deeper thoughts
options.C: It signals that the interview is officially over
options.D: It forces the participant to change the topic immediately

explanation: Spot on! Silence can feel awkward, but giving patients a moment to breathe lets them process deep emotions and share truly meaningful insights.

question: Which of these is a major use of a PET scan in cancer care (oncology)?

options.A: Staging cancer and checking if it has spread to other parts of the body.
options.B: Measuring the exact physical width and length of a bone fracture.
options.C: Checking the electrical rhythm of the heart during rest and exercise.
options.D: Removing small benign tumors without needing invasive surgery.

explanation: Spot on! Doctors rely heavily on PET scans to see how far cancer has traveled and whether treatments are working to shrink it.

question: What is the primary focus of gerontology?

options.A: The administration of emergency care in intensive care units
options.B: The study of aging and older adults from multiple disciplines
options.C: The surgical treatment of age-related bone fractures
options.D: The pharmacological management of childhood infectious diseases

explanation: Gerontology looks broadly at the physical, mental, and social changes that happen as people grow older. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h1)

question: What do we mean by 'donor fatigue' in international health financing?

options.A: Local nurses becoming too exhausted to complete shift handovers
options.B: International partners shifting their focus and funds to newer global crises
options.C: Government officials sleeping through parliamentary budget meetings
options.D: Patients refusing to take donated medications because they are expired

explanation: Donor fatigue happens when foreign funders lose interest or move their money to newer global emergencies, leaving older projects short of cash.

question: When does puerperal sepsis typically show up in a patient?

options.A: During the postpartum period
options.B: During the first trimester only
options.C: Five years after childbirth
options.D: Before the 12th week of pregnancy

explanation: You got it! Puerperal sepsis is a reproductive tract infection that develops after childbirth or a miscarriage, up to 42 days into the postpartum period.

question: What do we call the exercise where the nurse moves the patient's joint for them, without the patient doing any work?

options.A: Active-assisted movement
options.B: Passive range-of-motion exercise
options.C: Isometric muscle contraction
options.D: Resistive weight-training exercise

explanation: Correct! 'Passive' means the patient is relaxed while you do the moving to keep their joints nice and flexible.

question: What is the most important thing for a nurse to check right after giving a nebulizer treatment with a beta-agonist?

options.A: Checking the patient for signs of severe weight gain
options.B: Reassessing lung sounds and respiratory effort
options.C: Offering the patient a heavy, high-sodium meal
options.D: Inspecting the skin for signs of bruising or rashes

explanation: Always close the loop! Listening to the patient's lungs afterward lets you know right away if the medication did its job and made breathing easier.

question: What does having an 'appreciation for a system' mean in a busy hospital setting?

options.A: Ensuring every single department makes a profit
options.B: Keeping hospital departments strictly separated so no one gets distracted
options.C: Recognizing how different departments depend on each other to reach a common goal
options.D: Giving regular awards to hardworking nursing staff

explanation: Think of a hospital like a football team—pharmacy, lab, and nursing all have to pass the ball to each other to win for the patient!

question: What is the best immediate nursing action for an unconscious patient who is breathing on their own?

options.A: Force fluids by mouth to prevent dehydration during sleep
options.B: Place them in the recovery position to keep the airway clear
options.C: Prop them upright in bed to encourage deep lung breathing
options.D: Tie their arms to the bed rails to prevent sudden movement

explanation: The recovery position keeps the tongue from blocking the airway and lets saliva drain out safely. A classic life-saving nursing skill!

question: How does mindfulness meditation help people dealing with racing thoughts?

options.A: By teaching them to observe thoughts without judgment
options.B: By permanently erasing painful memories from the brain
options.C: By replacing emotional feelings with physical movement
options.D: By forcing the mind to stop thinking completely

explanation: Mindfulness isn't about clearing your head completely—it's about noticing your thoughts in the present moment without beating yourself up over them.

question: What is the main job of the aqueous humor in the eye?

options.A: Supplying nutrients and maintaining eye pressure
options.B: Converting light waves into electrical nerve impulses
options.C: Producing the colored pigments found in the iris
options.D: Adjusting the eye focus for very distant objects

explanation: Think of the aqueous humor as a nourishing liquid bath for the front of your eye, keeping it healthy and properly inflated.

question: When the baby's head is tucked down nicely (fully flexed), what is the measurement of the suboccipitobregmatic diameter?

options.D: 9.5 cm

explanation: You've got it! At 9.5 cm, this is the smallest and most comfortable measurement for a smooth journey through the pelvis.

question: How should a nurse handle someone who argues that there is 'no budget' for a new health project?

options.A: Ignore the stakeholder completely and proceed without their approval
options.B: Provide evidence showing financial losses caused by ignoring the issue
options.C: Offer to pay for the entire project out of the nurse's own salary
options.D: Argue loudly that the government is corrupt and does not care

explanation: Smart move! Showing them how much money the problem is *already* costing them helps turn a 'no budget' excuse into a reason to invest.

question: Why must nurses be careful about continuous patient surveillance in clinical spaces?

options.A: Doctors are not legally allowed to look at video feeds
options.B: Cameras use up too much electricity in the hospital room
options.C: It can make patients feel vulnerable and invade their privacy
options.D: Patients will stop sleeping and watch the cameras all night

explanation: Constant monitoring can compromise personal dignity if not balanced carefully with patient comfort and consent. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is required for a patient's informed consent to be legally valid?

options.A: A complete guarantee of a successful medical outcome
options.B: Direct verbal instruction from the lead hospital consultant
options.C: Written approval witnessed by a hospital lawyer
options.D: Voluntary agreement without force or pressure

explanation: Spot on! True consent must be given freely by the patient without any form of manipulation or coercion.

question: Why is proper documentation of a referral important for the client's care?

options.A: It proves to the government that the nurse worked extra hours
options.B: It prevents the receiving facility from repeating unnecessary assessments
options.C: It allows the nurse to charge extra administrative fees to the client
options.D: It stops the client from ever returning to the primary health center

explanation: Clear notes on clinical history and vital signs save time and guide the receiving team straight to appropriate management. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h5)

question: Which macronutrient is the body's go-to and fastest source of energy?

options.A: Fats
options.B: Proteins
options.C: Carbohydrates
options.D: Water

explanation: Carbs are your body's preferred energy food. They break down quickly into glucose to give you the energy you need for lectures and ward rounds!

question: You want to score how well nursing students perform sterile wound dressings in simulation. Which tool fits best?

options.A: An open-ended diary for students to write about their feelings
options.B: A simple task checklist that only records yes or no without scoring
options.C: A demographic questionnaire about the students' previous degrees
options.D: An evaluation or rating checklist to score the quality of performance

explanation: A rating checklist lets you assess how *well* a skill was done, going beyond a simple yes-or-no tick.

question: What is the popular local name for the skin boils caused by tumbu fly larvae in West Africa?

options.A: Guinea worm blister
options.B: Ground itch
options.C: Mango fly boil or 'tsoro'
options.D: Jigger foot

explanation: Tumbu fly larvae burrow under the skin to form raised, boil-like sores that locals commonly call mango fly boils or 'tsoro'. Excellent local clinical context!

question: Why is keeping accurate and timely nursing notes so important in peri-operative care?

options.A: It allows the patient to perform their own dressing changes.
options.B: It provides a clear legal record of the care provided.
options.C: It replaces the need for verbal handovers between shifts.
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital receives full financial grants.

explanation: Good medical records act as legal proof in court, showing that you delivered safe, standard care at the right time.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical role of the nurse during the implementation phase?

options.A: Motivating volunteers when the work gets difficult
options.B: Coordinating activities between different groups
options.C: Acting as a strict dictator who punishes lazy workers
options.D: Providing technical advice on health procedures

explanation: Nurses act as facilitators, advisors, and motivators, not as authoritarian bosses who punish community members. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h6)

question: What is the typical length of antibiotic treatment for osteomyelitis?

options.A: Four to six weeks or longer
options.B: Exactly 24 hours
options.C: Six months to one year
options.D: Three to five days

explanation: Because it's tricky for drugs to get deep inside hard bone tissue, patients need a nice long course of antibiotics—usually 4 to 6 weeks or even more.

question: When should you definitely reach for good old soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.B: Immediately after removing clean non-sterile gloves
options.C: Before touching a client who has a respiratory illness
options.D: When entering a home where clean water is expensive

explanation: You got it! Hand sanitisers are great, but if your hands have physical dirt or fluids on them, you need a proper wash with soap and water.

question: A newly qualified staff nurse guides a student on proper wound dressing technique. What does this situation demonstrate?

options.A: Formal ward management
options.B: Strict administrative control
options.C: Delegation of illegal tasks
options.D: Everyday nursing leadership

explanation: Guiding and teaching colleagues during clinical care is a form of leadership that any nurse can and should practice. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of these everyday activities is a classic example of NEAT (Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis)?

options.A: Running a scheduled marathon on Saturday morning
options.B: Lifting heavy weights at the gym for an hour
options.C: Pacing up and down the hospital hallway while on duty
options.D: Swimming laps in a competitive swimming pool

explanation: Exactly! As student nurses on clinical duty, all that walking, pacing, and running around the ward counts as NEAT—unplanned movement outside the gym!

question: What is a practical, budget-friendly nursing tip for a patient who cannot afford fresh vegetables?

options.A: Advise them to forage for wild plants in local public parks
options.B: Telling them to skip vegetables entirely until they find more money
options.C: Suggesting nutritious frozen vegetables or rinsed canned options
options.D: Insisting they only buy organic produce from specialty markets

explanation: Well done! Frozen and canned veggies are affordable, last longer, and still offer great nutrition when money is tight.

question: A patient takes a normal dose of a drug and gets unexpected liver failure that isn't an allergy. How should you classify this as a nurse?

options.A: A mild side effect of therapy
options.B: An idiosyncratic reaction
options.C: A predictable drug toxicity
options.D: A standard allergic response

explanation: Since it happened at a normal dose and wasn't an allergy or standard toxicity, it's a classic rare idiosyncrasy. Well reasoned!

question: What is the recommended infant feeding practice for mothers living on ART where replacement feeding is unsafe?

options.A: Exclusive use of herbal teas and plain water
options.B: Immediate weaning onto cow milk on day one
options.C: Strict formula feeding without any breast milk
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding combined with maternal ART provides the best balance of nutrition and protection against HIV transmission. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h7)

question: Why do we keep our fingers pointing upward or straight down toward the sink drain when rinsing our hands?

options.A: To help the soap lather faster under the faucet stream
options.B: To allow the wrist veins to cool down during scrubbing
options.C: To keep the paper towels from getting wet too early
options.D: To prevent contaminated water from running back up the clean arms

explanation: Gravity is on your side when you keep fingers pointing down—it ensures dirty water flows away from your clean arms and straight down the drain.

question: During a routine screening test where the cervix is inspected visually using acetic acid (VIA), what is acetic acid actually made of?

options.A: Normal saline
options.B: Dilute vinegar
options.C: Betadine solution
options.D: Hydrogen peroxide

explanation: You got it! Acetic acid is just dilute vinegar. When applied to the cervix, it causes abnormal, protein-packed cells to turn white so the nurse or doctor can easily spot them.

question: A patient is having a rising panic attack at home. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink several cups of strong coffee
options.B: Scold the patient for worrying over unimportant matters
options.C: Leave the patient completely alone in a dark room until they calm down
options.D: Guide the patient through slow, deep breathing exercises

explanation: Brilliant! Slow, steady breaths help lower the heart rate and calm down hyperventilation. Nursing care at its finest!

question: Why is it important for clinical nurses to be involved when designing new health software?

options.A: To write the computer programming code and fix hardware bugs
options.B: To replace hospital administrators during board meetings
options.C: To ensure the technology actually matches real-world bedside workflows
options.D: To market the software to other hospitals for profit

explanation: Involving nurses ensures that digital systems are practical and helpful in actual clinical practice rather than creating unnecessary obstacles. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which class of medication is usually given first for obsessive-compulsive neurosis?

options.A: Tricyclic muscle relaxants
options.B: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors
options.C: Short-acting barbiturate sedatives
options.D: Atypical antipsychotic medications

explanation: You got it! SSRIs are the go-to drugs to help balance serotonin levels and dial down those intense symptoms.

question: Which of these is a key part of doing a full, holistic nursing assessment?

options.A: Exploring the patient's home support systems and cultural beliefs
options.B: Avoiding questions about mental health to prevent upsetting them
options.C: Rushing the patient to finish answering interview questions quickly
options.D: Focusing exclusively on laboratory values and bedside monitors

explanation: Awesome! Holistic assessments intentionally gather data on social, cultural, and emotional factors right alongside physical signs.

question: Which part of the nephron reabsorbs the biggest share of filtered bicarbonate?

options.A: Loop of Henle
options.B: Distal convoluted tubule
options.C: Collecting duct
options.D: Proximal convoluted tubule

explanation: You've got this! The proximal convoluted tubule is the hardworking champion that reclaims the vast majority of filtered bicarbonate right back into the bloodstream.

question: How do the HPV proteins known as E6 and E7 actually cause trouble in the body's cells?

options.A: Deactivate tumor suppressor proteins like p53 and Rb
options.B: Increase local tissue oxygenation
options.C: Stimulate rapid production of red blood cells
options.D: Strengthen the basement membrane of the cervix

explanation: Great try! Normally, our bodies have defense proteins (like p53 and Rb) that stop damaged cells from multiplying. High-risk HPV produces E6 and E7 proteins that switch these defenses off, letting abnormal cells grow unchecked.

question: How does hematogenous osteomyelitis differ from contiguous osteomyelitis?

options.A: Hematogenous only affects the skull, while contiguous affects long bones exclusively
options.B: Hematogenous is caused by viruses, whereas contiguous is always caused by fungi
options.C: Hematogenous spreads through the bloodstream, while contiguous comes from a nearby open wound or infection
options.D: Hematogenous occurs only in older adults, while contiguous is strictly pediatric

explanation: Think of 'hematogenous' as hitching a ride through the blood from somewhere else in the body, while 'contiguous' means the infection touched the bone directly from an outside wound nearby.

question: Which mental health challenges most commonly first appear during the teenage years?

options.A: Senile dementia and delirium
options.B: Post-partum psychosis
options.C: Depression and anxiety
options.D: Severe cognitive regression

explanation: Well done! Because of all the massive body changes and social stress, depression and anxiety often peak or first show up during these years.

question: How do unit managers usually help with hospital budgeting?

options.A: By setting the salaries for all doctors in the country
options.B: By deciding which private bank holds hospital funds
options.C: By predicting future equipment and supply needs for their ward
options.D: By collecting taxes from patients upon discharge

explanation: Great thinking! Managers know their wards best, so they help the finance team by forecasting what materials and tools their department will need.

question: What is a very common local belief about injected medications compared to pills?

options.A: Pills are absorbed directly into the bloodstream
options.B: Pills are always more expensive than injections
options.C: Injections have zero risk of side effects
options.D: Injections are believed to work faster and more powerfully

explanation: That's right! Many people hold the myth that injections are stronger magic because they go straight into the body.

question: Why can deep-seated traditional beliefs sometimes cause trouble for NGO health outreaches?

options.A: Communities may be suspicious of external medical workers and prefer local practices
options.B: Local elders legally prohibit nurses from administering vaccines
options.C: Traditional beliefs automatically provide all necessary surgical supplies
options.D: Culture prevents community members from ever falling ill

explanation: If an NGO just shows up without talking to the community first, residents might be suspicious. Building trust is always step one!

question: Why must certain antiretroviral drugs be taken alongside food?

options.A: To stop the patient from feeling hungry at night
options.B: To replace drinking clean water
options.C: To reduce stomach irritation and improve drug absorption
options.D: To destroy the outer tablet coating instantly

explanation: You nailed it! Some meds are much easier on the stomach and work better when taken with a meal or snack.

question: Which statistical test should you use to compare the average scores of two completely separate groups of patients?

options.A: Descriptive median
options.B: Independent t-test
options.C: Chi-square test
options.D: Paired t-test

explanation: Spot on! When your two groups are totally separate (like Ward A patients vs. Ward B patients), an independent t-test is your go-to tool.

question: Why must a nurse flush a feeding tube before and after giving medication or formula?

options.A: To cool down the internal stomach lining
options.B: To stimulate natural saliva production
options.C: To prevent the tube from clogging
options.D: To increase the patient's daily water weight

explanation: Feeding tubes are narrow and can easily block up with thick formula or crushed meds. A simple water flush keeps everything flowing smoothly.

question: What do we call the mature, fluid-filled follicle that is fully ready to release an egg?

options.A: Corpus albicans
options.B: Primordial follicle
options.C: Graafian follicle
options.D: Atretic follicle

explanation: The Graafian follicle is the final, mature stage before it bursts open to release the egg. Great landmark to remember in reproductive anatomy!

question: What is the main goal of routine GI screenings like a colonoscopy?

options.A: To cure existing advanced infections instantly without medicine
options.B: To detect polyps and early-stage cancer before symptoms start
options.C: To measure the exact daily caloric intake of the patient
options.D: To replace the need for healthy eating and hydration

explanation: Screening lets doctors catch tiny growths or early changes long before they turn into major problems.

question: Legally speaking, what happens if you perform a nursing care action but forget to write it down?

options.A: The patient must pay a fine for incomplete medical records
options.B: Legally, the care is considered not to have been done
options.C: The physician takes full responsibility for the omitted note
options.D: The hospital automatically waives all liability for the event

explanation: That's right! In a court of law, if it isn't documented, it never happened. Remember: if you did it, chart it!

question: What is the main difference between vehicle-borne and vector-borne transmission?

options.A: Vehicle transmission is restricted strictly to airborne droplet nuclei.
options.B: Vehicle transmission requires direct physical contact between humans.
options.C: Vector transmission only occurs through contaminated food and water supplies.
options.D: Vehicle transmission involves non-living objects, while vector transmission involves living organisms.

explanation: Spot on! Vehicles are non-living things like water or food, while vectors are living creatures like insects.

question: How does food intoxication differ from a food infection?

options.A: Intoxication only affects the upper respiratory system
options.B: Infection has a much shorter incubation period
options.C: Infection is caused strictly by chemical pollutants
options.D: Intoxication results from pre-formed toxins in the food

explanation: Think of food intoxication as getting sick from poisons that bacteria already made inside the food before you ate it, leading to very fast symptoms!

question: Which of these devices is a great example of therapeutic equipment used to treat a patient?

options.A: ECG machine
options.B: Nebulizer
options.C: Thermometer
options.D: Stethoscope

explanation: Therapeutic equipment actively helps treat conditions and aids recovery. A nebulizer does this brilliantly by delivering medication straight to the airways!

question: A patient experiences heavy monthly bleeding and cramping as the inner lining of her uterus sheds. Which layer is primarily involved?

options.A: Myometrium
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Cervical stroma
options.D: Perimetrium

explanation: The endometrium is the inner mucosal lining that builds up and sheds every month during menstruation. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h3)

question: What crucial information must you always write down in a patient's referral note?

options.A: The religious affiliation and family history of the patient
options.B: A detailed breakdown of transport costs incurred by the family
options.C: The personal phone number of the community health officer
options.D: Vital signs, suspected diagnosis, and treatment given so far

explanation: The receiving doctors need a quick cheat sheet! Always include current vital signs, what you think is wrong, and any drugs or fluids you've already given.

question: Why does having more sex hormone-binding globulin mean less active testosterone?

options.A: It binds to testosterone so tissues cannot use it
options.B: It blocks the pituitary gland from releasing luteinizing hormone
options.C: It speeds up the clearance of testosterone through the kidneys
options.D: It destroys the testosterone molecules completely

explanation: Think of sex hormone-binding globulin like a pair of handcuffs. Once it attaches to testosterone, the hormone is locked up and cannot do its usual job in the body.

question: As a nurse assessing a patient with severe iron-deficiency anemia, what physical sign are you most likely to spot?

options.A: Pallor of the mucous membranes and nail beds
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes
options.C: Swelling in the hands and lower feet
options.D: Rapid and excessive involuntary weight gain

explanation: Great clinical eye! Low hemoglobin means fewer red blood cells, which makes the inner eyelids, gums, and nail beds look pale.

question: How does the way a baby is born affect their early microbiome?

options.A: Cesarean delivery guarantees total sterility of the infant gut for months
options.B: Vaginal birth prevents any beneficial bacteria from entering the body
options.C: Vaginal birth exposes the baby to maternal vaginal and gut flora
options.D: Delivery method has zero impact on the microbial colonization process

explanation: Babies born vaginally pick up helpful microbes directly from the mother's birth canal, while babies born via CS-section pick up more skin and environmental microbes first. Every baby's start is unique!

question: What is the main goal of doing a 'review of systems' during an assessment?

options.A: To perform the physical examination using diagnostic instruments
options.B: To uncover symptoms the patient may have forgotten or omitted
options.C: To measure objective laboratory values and blood counts
options.D: To establish the legal billing code for the clinic visit

explanation: Spot on! It acts as a safety net to catch any little health issues the patient didn't think to bring up earlier.

question: What is a great benefit of building an open safety culture in a healthcare facility?

options.A: The hospital completely eliminates all forms of clinical illness
options.B: Staff feel safe reporting near-misses so errors can be prevented
options.C: Patients stop asking questions about their medications
options.D: Senior nurses no longer need to check any patient charts

explanation: When staff feel comfortable speaking up about close calls ('near-misses'), the team can fix them before any actual harm reaches the patient.

question: Why do we perform a crossmatch test before giving a blood transfusion?

options.A: To check for direct reactions between donor cells and recipient serum
options.B: To measure the exact volume of red blood cells in the patient
options.C: To find out if the patient has any hidden infectious diseases
options.D: To determine the patient's baseline hemoglobin and hematocrit

explanation: Crossmatching is a crucial safety step! Lab staff mix donor cells and recipient serum together first to make sure they won't react violently inside the patient's body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h4)

question: According to standard color-coding rules, which bin color is used for infectious waste?

options.A: Yellow with a biohazard symbol
options.B: Bright metallic silver
options.C: Plain black or brown
options.D: See-through clear plastic

explanation: Bright yellow bins marked with the biohazard sign are universally used to warn everyone and collect infectious or pathological waste.

question: Who is the expert behind the System of Profound Knowledge framework?

options.A: Jean Watson
options.B: W. Edwards Deming
options.C: Florence Nightingale
options.D: Abraham Maslow

explanation: W. Edwards Deming created this framework to help workplaces improve continuously and make quality care easier for everyone.

question: Which physical item should the nurse inspect to evaluate medication adherence at home?

options.A: The electrical sockets for signs of dangerous overloading
options.B: The pill bottles or containers to check remaining doses
options.C: The family photo albums on the living room shelves
options.D: The kitchen trash can for discarded food wrappers

explanation: Inspecting medication packaging helps verify whether the client is actually taking their prescribed drugs on schedule. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why is early contraceptive counseling crucial immediately following abortion treatment?

options.A: Because hormonal contraceptives immediately cure any underlying uterine infections
options.B: Because ovulation can return as early as two weeks after an abortion
options.C: Because federal law mandates contraceptive use before hospital discharge
options.D: Because patients lose their fertility permanently if they wait one month

explanation: That's right! A woman can get pregnant again very quickly, even before her first normal period returns, making immediate counseling essential.

question: What exactly is an epitope?

options.A: A chemical substance released by damaged skin tissue
options.B: The specific part of an antigen that immune receptors bind to
options.C: A large white blood cell found inside the lymph nodes
options.D: The protective protein coat surrounding a harmful virus

explanation: Think of an epitope as the specific handle or tag on a germ that immune cells grab onto.

question: What is the primary goal of primary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Stopping health problems before they ever start
options.B: Screening for early signs of hidden cancer
options.C: Rehabilitating patients after a major stroke
options.D: Treating advanced chronic diseases with surgery

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on risk reduction and health education to prevent a condition from developing in the first place. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h4)

question: Which part of the ear contains the special structures that handle both your hearing and your sense of balance?

options.A: The middle ear
options.B: The inner ear
options.C: The outer ear
options.D: The external canal

explanation: Spot on! The inner ear houses the cochlea for hearing and the semicircular canals for keeping your balance.

question: What is a flat, colored spot on the skin that is less than 1 cm wide called?

options.A: Papule
options.B: Plaque
options.C: Vesicle
options.D: Macule

explanation: Think of a simple freckle or flat mole—that's a macule! It's just a flat, colored spot on the skin.

question: What happens to most people who catch the poliovirus?

options.A: They experience severe respiratory failure
options.B: They show no symptoms at all
options.C: They suffer from chronic diarrhea
options.D: They develop permanent paralysis

explanation: Surprise! The vast majority of people infected with polio feel completely fine, which is why it can spread so silently in communities.

question: Which portion of a fat-soluble hormone in the blood is actually active and able to affect cells?

options.A: The large fraction securely attached to liver carrier proteins
options.B: The small fraction that remains unbound or free in the blood
options.C: The portion that gets trapped inside blood vessel walls
options.D: The total amount secreted by the endocrine gland combined

explanation: Only the free, unattached hormones can slip out of the blood vessels to do their job. The rest stay safely hitched to their carrier proteins like passengers on a bus!

question: Why are nurses often the best members of the healthcare team to give dietary advice?

options.A: They spend the most direct time with patients and understand their daily routines
options.B: They control the hospital food supply chain and kitchen staff
options.C: They have legal authority to write formal diet prescription orders
options.D: They are the only healthcare workers trained in human biochemistry

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses spend the most time with patients, we really get to know their daily lives and routines, making our advice much more practical.

question: Which protein choice is best and safest for a strict low-fat diet?

options.A: Full-fat cheddar cheese
options.B: Marmbled beef steak
options.C: Fried catfish fillets
options.D: Skinless chicken breast

explanation: You got it! Skinless poultry is very lean and low in fat, making it a staple for low-fat meal plans.

question: How do everyday stressors affect the development of neurasthenia?

options.A: They permanently alter brain chemistry instantly
options.B: They prevent any form of physical illness from occurring
options.C: They deplete coping reserves over time and trigger exhaustion
options.D: They have no impact on mental or physical health

explanation: You nailed it! Constant daily pressure slowly drains a person's nervous energy until they feel totally burnt out. Keep going!

question: A patient with high cholesterol asks which fat to avoid completely. What should you tell them?

options.A: Trans fats
options.B: Omega-3 fatty acids
options.C: Polyunsaturated oils
options.D: Monounsaturated fats

explanation: Trans fats are artificial troublemakers! They raise bad cholesterol and lower the good kind, so it's best to avoid them for a healthy heart.

question: What is eutrophication in plain terms?

options.A: A sudden increase of clean mineral nutrients in underground wells
options.B: The natural warming of river water by industrial thermal plants
options.C: Oxygen depletion in water caused by the decomposition of excess algae
options.D: The direct filtration of heavy metals through sandy soil layers

explanation: You got it! Too many nutrients cause massive algae blooms; when those plants die and rot, they suck all the oxygen out of the water.

question: Which phase of a rescue operation involves sweeping the disaster area to find where victims are trapped?

options.A: Stabilization
options.B: Localization
options.C: Extrication
options.D: Evacuation

explanation: Think of localization as the mapping and finding stage. Teams use tools, dogs, and visual sweeps to spot exactly where trapped people are.

question: What happens when strategic, tactical, and operational plans fail to align in a hospital?

options.A: Long-term goals are achieved much faster
options.B: Daily nursing tasks become completely automated
options.C: Staff frustration increases and patient care suffers
options.D: The hospital automatically runs more efficiently

explanation: A disconnect between management levels creates confusion, wasted effort, and poor outcomes for patients. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the main advantage of using secondary data in nursing research?

options.A: It saves time and resources because someone else already collected it
options.B: It gives the researcher total control over how questions are asked
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any statistical analysis
options.D: It guarantees that there will be zero errors in the dataset

explanation: Secondary data lets researchers study large topics quickly using existing records without setting up new data collection projects. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h4)

question: What does professional accountability primarily require of a nurse?

options.A: Avoid reporting clinical errors made by colleagues
options.B: Make all financial decisions for the hospital ward
options.C: Supervise every task performed by junior medical doctors
options.D: Answer for their own actions and accept the consequences

explanation: You've got this! Accountability simply means owning your clinical choices, standing by your actions, and accepting the outcomes like a true professional.

question: What do we call an infection that a patient picks up while receiving care in a hospital?

options.A: An allergic reaction to medication given during a surgical procedure
options.B: A chronic disease that worsens over many years of outpatient visits
options.C: Any illness a person brings into the hospital from their home environment
options.D: An infection a patient catches while inside a medical facility for care

explanation: You got it! These are known as healthcare-associated infections (HAIs), meaning they weren't there when the patient first arrived.

question: A male patient is diagnosed with an indirect inguinal hernia. Which nearby anatomical structure is most at risk of compression within the inguinal canal?

options.A: Spermatic cord contents
options.B: Corporis cavernosa
options.C: Urinary bladder neck
options.D: Bulbourethral glands

explanation: Because the spermatic cord passes directly through the inguinal canal, a hernia in this area can compress the vessels and nerves within the cord. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient had her right fallopian tube removed three years ago due to a severe infection. How is this absence classified?

options.A: Congenital agenesis
options.B: Acquired absence
options.C: Müllerian dysgenesis
options.D: Primary tubal hypoplasia

explanation: You got it! Because the tube was present originally and lost later due to surgery or disease, it's an 'acquired' condition.

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluating a health communication program?

options.A: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is always completely free
options.B: Monitoring is done by patients, while evaluation is done by politicians
options.C: Monitoring tracks daily activities, while evaluation measures long-term impact
options.D: Monitoring focuses on drugs, while evaluation focuses only on surgery

explanation: Well done! Monitoring looks at what is happening day-to-day, while evaluation checks the overall success at the end.

question: What is the main reason doctors order a daily 'sedation vacation' for a ventilated patient?

options.A: To let the ventilator machine calibrate its internal sensors
options.B: To allow the nursing staff to take a scheduled meal break
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of medications in the unit
options.D: To evaluate the patient's neurological status and readiness for weaning

explanation: Pausing sedation for a short while lets us check how the patient's brain is doing and see if they are strong enough to start breathing on their own. Brilliant teamwork!

question: Which surveillance type relies on healthcare workers sending routine reports without special prompting?

options.A: Active surveillance
options.B: Sentinel surveillance
options.C: Passive surveillance
options.D: Syndromic surveillance

explanation: Passive surveillance relies on routine reporting by clinics and hospitals without outside prompting, making it simple but prone to underreporting. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h2)

question: What is the main job of iron in the human body?

options.A: To digest dietary fats in the stomach
options.B: To form hemoglobin in red blood cells for oxygen transport
options.C: To regulate body temperature during a fever
options.D: To provide immediate energy for running

explanation: Iron forms the core of hemoglobin—the protein that acts like a delivery truck, carrying oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.

question: Which type of female genital mutilation involves cutting and narrowing the vaginal opening?

options.A: Type IV unclassified
options.B: Type II excision
options.C: Type III infibulation
options.D: Type I clitoridectomy

explanation: Great job! Type III (infibulation) is the most severe form, creating a seal over the opening and leaving just a tiny space for urine and monthly flow.

question: Which of these actions does NOT support safe patient care by a nurse leader?

options.A: Maintaining adequate staffing levels for patient acuity
options.B: Ensuring evidence-based clinical guidelines are followed
options.C: Punishing staff publicly for reporting near-misses
options.D: Promoting open communication and incident reporting

explanation: Spot on! Publicly punishing staff for speaking up only creates fear, making people hide their mistakes and putting patients at greater risk.

question: Which nerve supplies the main feeling and sensation to the external female genitalia?

options.A: The obturator nerve
options.B: The femoral nerve
options.C: The pudendal nerve
options.D: The sciatic nerve

explanation: Great recall! The pudendal nerve is the main pathway supplying feeling to the perineum and external genitalia.

question: Why is it important to test draft survey questions on a small group before the main study?

options.A: To force participants to agree with the researcher
options.B: To finish the research project much faster
options.C: To catch hidden mistakes and confusing wording
options.D: To make the final paper look longer and better

explanation: Pilot testing helps identify confusing questions and errors before you spend time and resources on the full study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h4)

question: Which Nigerian federal agency enforces environmental standards, including healthcare waste rules?

options.A: FRSC
options.B: NESREA
options.C: NYSC
options.D: NAPTIP

explanation: That's right! NESREA is the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency in Nigeria. You're doing brilliantly!

question: In the SMART criteria for writing good objectives, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Measurable
options.B: Methodological
options.C: Medical
options.D: Mandatory

explanation: The 'M' stands for Measurable. It ensures your objective includes clear indicators you can actually count, observe, or evaluate! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h5)

question: Which of these commonly causes frustration when using mobile nursing technology on the ward?

options.A: Too many physical stairs in modern multi-story hospitals
options.B: Dead batteries and poor wireless internet connectivity
options.C: Patients demanding to program the IV pumps themselves
options.D: Doctors refusing to let nurses touch computer carts

explanation: So true! Nothing slows down a shift quite like a dying battery or a spinning loading wheel when you're trying to chart quickly.

question: During drug breakdown, what actually happens in a chemical process called hydrolysis?

options.A: Hydrogen atoms are removed to increase drug activity
options.B: A chemical bond is split by adding a water molecule
